channel.title: Sprezzature — Release notes
channel.description: Combined, date-sorted release notes from the sprezzature-* packages (accessibility, audio, CLI-to-GUI, colors, figures, maps, UX laws) and the main sprezzature skills repository.

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.19.0: the GUI stops asking Google for its typefaces
item.description: Fixed **The gallery page fetched all three Roboto families from `fonts.googleapis.com` on every load.** Three tags at the top of `gui.py` -- two `preconnect` hints and a stylesheet link -- in a package that otherwise needs no network at all: it draws from vendored rasters, and the suite routes even its model calls through a local Ollama. A reader offline, or behind a filter, got the page set in whatever their machine happened to own. …

item.title: sprezzature-figures 2.7.0: the wheel carries every face the module offers
item.description: **Roboto Serif is back in the wheel, and the wheel grows 3.4 MB to 11.4 MB for it.** That is the whole release: a typography decision reversing a packaging one, plus the test that should have been there to make the disagreement impossible. 2.6.0 narrowed the font package-data to drop Roboto Serif -- 12.2 MB of 18.6 uncompressed, for a family neither theme sets. The saving was real and the reasoning was sound. What made it a defect is that `fonts.py` went on offering `serif` and `serif_italic` anyway, so the module advertised ten faces while the wheel carried eight, and **nothing in this repository could tell**: the source tree's `assets/fonts/` holds every face regardless of what a build contains, so every font path passes locally by construction. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.18.0: a page a journal can actually use
item.description: Added **`--out plate.pdf` and `--out plate.eps` write a drawn page.** Every journal that asks for PDF or EPS is asking for vector; what shipped was a PNG in a PDF wrapper, which satisfies the extension and nothing else, and which nobody can tell from the real thing until they zoom in -- by which point the figure is in review. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.17.1: a key that filled its width with whitespace
item.description: Fixed **The legend band sized every column for the longest label in the whole key.** A key of three short rows and one long one laid `RSF` out in a 252-unit column of which it used 46, did that three times across the band, and pushed the long row onto a second line the band had room for. The complaint it was logged under was that the band did not fill its width; the render says the opposite and is the one to believe. It filled the width with whitespace, which is the version that reads as broken. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.17.0: a plate that can prove which inputs drew it
item.description: Added **`provenance`: the question a caption cannot settle.** A plate already prints `method`, `source` and `as_of` — what it was drawn from, in prose, for a reader. None of that answers what review actually asks of a published figure: *is this the picture these inputs produce?* The drawing is a function of three things — the code, the config, and the file a loader read on the way in — and `provenance: true` fingerprints each of them into `<metadata>`, so that a mismatch later says **which one moved** instead of leaving a reviewer to guess. …

item.title: sprezzature-figures 2.6.0: forty figures, and the probe that found what the catalogue only claimed
item.description: 2.5.0 was prepared in this repository and never reached PyPI, so 2.6.0 is the first release carrying it. Everything in the 2.5.0 section below ships here. The catalogue goes from **127 kinds to 167**, additively: nothing was removed, nothing was renamed. But the headline of this release is not the count. It is that writing forty figures in a row produced a probe, and the probe found that a large part of the *existing* catalogue had been advertising options it silently ignored. Added **Forty new kinds.** By family: *Distributions and fields* — `hist2d`, `contour`, `tricontour`, `trisurface`, `voxels`, `quiver3d`, `line3d`. *Time and sequence* — `acf`, `seasonal-decomposition`, `forecast-fan`, `control-chart`, `ohlc`, `bump`, `stem`, `eventplot`, `sparkline`, `dual-axis`. …

item.title: sprezzature 1.4.0: `sprezzature[all]` could not install, and every page undercounted the catalogue by forty
item.description: Changed **`best-engine-ai-helper` is no longer presented as part of the suite.** It belongs to the `ai-helpers` family, not to this one: it has its own repository, its own release line on PyPI, and it serves projects that have nothing to do with sprezzature. Folding it in cost it that audience and made this suite look like it owned a runtime it merely calls. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.16.0: the same plate once per window, and a key that drew one symbol in three
item.description: Added **`small_multiples`: one panel per window of time.** A situation plate is a snapshot, and most of what research says about a conflict is a change. The two usual answers both give something away. An animation asks the reader to compare a frame against one they can no longer see. One plate exported per window lets the extent, the projection and the symbol scale drift apart between frames, with nothing on the page admitting that the panels have stopped being comparable. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.15.0: fifty-five silent tab stops, and a plate that could not be printed
item.description: Two defects that a rendered picture cannot show, because neither of them is visible. The plates look exactly as they did. Fixed **The legend key drew a symbol the plate did not.** `marker_legend` rows were hardcoded to precision 1, so an aggregated plate showed a solid disc in its key beside marks that were all hollow broken rings — the same page teaching the colour correctly and the symbol wrongly. Found by rendering an aggregated plate and looking at its legend. …

item.description: Added …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.13.0: eight names printed on top of each other, twelve drawn where no reader gets them, and a ruler that was wrong about every capital letter
item.description: Every placement defect this repository has ever fixed was found by rendering a plate and looking at it. That finds the plate you looked at and the defect you looked for. This release measures the finished SVG instead -- walks the markup, composes the ancestor transforms, and asks where every visible word actually lands -- and the first run of it found eight collisions and three invisible labels across the nine bundled plates, none of which any of the 243 existing tests could see. Fixed …

item.title: sprezzature-figures 2.5.0: every figure's own options, on the command line and over HTTP
item.description: Each of the 127 generators is a function with a signature — `make_bar(data, *, out, title, subtitle, width, height, mode, accessibility, language, x_label, y_label, theme)`. A library caller could read it and pass what it wanted. A command-line caller could pass `--title`, and nothing else. An HTTP caller could send an `options` object that was never checked, so a misspelt key was dropped on the way in and the figure came back looking as though it had ignored the request. That surface is now derived from the generators themselves and published through all three doors. Added …

item.title: sprezzature-ux-laws 1.1.0: the auditor is installable, which is the whole package
item.description: Two changelog sections sat under "Unreleased" since August and September. They ship here, together with the release that makes the auditor reachable at all. Added **`sprezzature-ux-laws-audit`, a console script.** The auditor is this package's reason to exist and nothing installed it. The README told readers to run `python scripts/audit_laws_of_ux.py`, a path that exists in a clone and not in a wheel, and the parser's own `--help` advertised `sprezzature-ux-laws-audit`, which nothing registered. Someone who ran `pip install sprezzature-ux-laws` could reach the MCP server and nothing else. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.9.4: terrain you can see through the thematic fill
item.description: A Ralph Eyeball Loop on the physical layers — relief, lakes, rivers — and how they stack. Rendered, looked at, adjusted, looked at again. Changed — how terrain is composited Shading was drawn **underneath** everything, with the land polygon left translucent (`fill-opacity` 0.45) so it showed through. That works, and it costs two things it need not: the land colour is diluted towards whatever lies beneath it, so a warm cream basemap drifts cold and green; the shading is composited by alpha, so a dark valley lightens the paper as much as it darkens it — the opposite of what a shadow does. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.9.3: refuse what cannot be drawn honestly
item.description: Two more Ralph Loop passes, aimed at the inputs a real caller supplies rather than at the plates. The drawing code held up throughout; the **refusals** did not. The generators were careful about everything except the values they cannot work without. Fixed — the choropleth rendered data that did not exist **An empty result set became the demo.** `rows = data if data else DEMO_DATA` cannot tell `None` ("I brought nothing, show me the demo") from `[]` ("my query ran and returned no rows"). The plate's subtitle kept the simple case honest — it says "synthetic demo data" — but it is applied only when the caller supplied no subtitle, so ```python build_svg([], title="Q3 revenue by country", subtitle="Millions of euros") ``` …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.12.0: three defects a type gate found, one of them on every default map
item.description: This package was left out of the sweep that gave its six sibling packages a type gate on 2026-10-02. The miss was not free. Running mypy here for the first time stopped immediately on a sentence: a prose comment in `scripts/make_situation_map.py` opened a line with `# type:`, which PEP 484 reserves for type comments, so mypy read the sentence as an annotation, failed to parse it, and gave up on the file. Nothing reported this. The consequence is that `scripts/` had never been checked at all, and the three defects below had been sitting in it. 0.11.0 was prepared but never published; its changes ship here. Fixed …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.11.0: six maps nobody could rebuild, and a plateau that looked like a plain
item.description: The website's gallery carried twelve maps. Five had builders. The other seven — four situation plates, three choropleths — were rendered once in August, before this package was split out of the monorepo, and carried along as files ever since. When the 0.10.1 fix went out, the five with recipes were regenerated in one command and the rest were not, because nobody could. Rebuilding them meant looking hard at four plates whose entire subject is the physical base, and that turned up a run of things the conflict plates had been hiding. Added **Four reference plates with builders**: `switzerland`, `iberia`, `western-europe` (the one `SKILL.md` cites as its worked example) and `himalaya`. They carry no thematic layer on purpose — a reader looking at Ukraine is looking at the front line, and the terrain under it only has to stay out of the way. Here there is nothing else to look at. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.10.1: two factions that 0.10.0 silently deleted
item.description: 0.10.0 clipped control zones to land so a schematic rectangle would stop painting the sea. On two of the five shipped plates it deleted a whole faction instead, and the full suite stayed green. Fixed **Syria lost its government and Libya lost the NTC.** Damascus, Homs, Hama, Latakia, Tartus — the entire west and south of the Syrian plate — rendered as plain desert, indistinguishable from Turkey and Jordan beside it, on a map titled "Syria: Areas of Control". The legend went on promising both classes, because a legend swatch is drawn from the palette and never asks the geometry whether it made it to the page. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.10.0: the water is water, and the plate can be questioned
item.description: Two threads, both driven by rendering plates and looking at them. The natural layers had no shared logic, and the plate had no life on a page. New config keys and flags, in one place | Key | Where | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `interactivity` | top level | `"self-contained"` (default), `"external"`, `"static"` | | `areas_of_control.over_water` | bool, default `false` | keep a zone's own shape instead of clipping it to land | | `lakes.depth_rings` | int, default `4` | shelf rings stepped inward from a lake's shore; `0` is off | No CLI flag changes. `make_situation_map`'s module docstring now carries the complete key reference, enforced by `tests/test_config_schema_is_documented.py`. Fixed — a control zone painted the sea …

item.title: sprezzature-figures 2.4.0: a mismatched pair raises instead of drawing a shorter chart
item.description: Fixed **99 `zip()` calls said nothing about length, and 85 of them should have.** A `zip()` over two sequences stops at the shorter one. Where those sequences are parallel by construction (x against y, labels against values, centres against radii), a length that diverges meant the tail was dropped in silence and the figure still rendered, correct-looking and wrong. Those 85 now pass `strict=True` and raise instead. The remaining 14 are sliding pairs (`zip(xs, xs[1:])`) where the truncation is the point, and say `strict=False`. Ten generators already used `strict=True`: the convention existed and had never been carried through. This is the one change here a caller can feel. Data that silently lost its tail now stops with an error, which is the behaviour this package exists to provide, and is why this is a minor release rather than a patch. …

item.title: sprezzature-colors 1.0.1: the half of the dependency guard nobody runs
item.description: Fixed **`mcp.py` defined `main` twice, and the two took different arguments.** One definition sits in the `except ImportError` branch reached when the `[mcp]` extra is absent, the other in the `else` branch that serves the real endpoint. A single console script reaches both, so to a caller they are one function. They were not: the fallback took nothing while the real one took `argv`, so `main(["--host", "127.0.0.1"])` answered on a machine with the extra and raised `TypeError` on a machine without it. The broken half is the one a reader who skipped the extra meets first. **`harchaoui.org` is gone, and every reference pointed at it.** The host now answers 503; the links go to `deraison.ai` and `sprezzature.ai`, including the `project.urls` homepage PyPI prints on the package page. …

item.title: sprezzature 1.3.9: the package page told readers to install v1.0.0
item.description: Fixed **The install snippet named a version three minor releases old**, in all four places that show it: the English and French sites, the README and the LISEZMOI. Its comment said "set VERSION to the latest tag on the releases page", which names the work instead of doing it, and nobody had done it since 1.0.0. 1.3.8 shipped that README to PyPI, so the package page itself handed readers a stale tarball. The version is now resolved on the spot from the releases API, so the line cannot age again. Verified end to end in a throwaway directory: it resolves the current tag, downloads, extracts the ten skill folders, and the two targets of the next step's `cp` are there. This release exists to put that corrected README on the package page; a fix that only lands in git leaves the live page saying the wrong thing.

item.title: sprezzature 1.3.8: the one command that installs the suite was handing out old packages
item.description: Fixed **Every floor in the `all` extra named a version older than the release sitting beside it.** `pip install sprezzature[all]` is the one command that installs the whole suite, and a floor that lags a correction installs the uncorrected package forever. `sprezzature-maps` was the worst of them, floored at 0.7.0 against a checkout at 0.12.0, five releases behind. The floors now name the versions published today: figures 2.4.0, colors 1.0.1, accessibility 1.0.3, audio 1.1.1, cli-gui 1.1.0, ux-laws 1.1.0, maps 0.12.0. `tests/test_all_extra_is_the_suite.py` has been saying so and failing. It is the check for the machine that cuts the release, and it was right. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.9.2: a Ralph Loop over the whole project
item.description: Two iterations of render-it-and-look-at-it across every surface, not just the plates. The findings were mostly not in the drawing code, which is tested and looked at constantly; they were in everything that *describes* the drawing code, which nothing checks. Fixed **`density` was invisible on every surface that is written by hand.** The third generator has been real for a while — in the library, at `/v1/density`, in both CLIs, and in MCP as `render_density` — and it was absent from the GUI gallery (0 mentions in 5 522 bytes of HTML), from `EXAMPLES.md` (0 mentions in 162 lines), from both routing tables in `TRIGGERS.md`, and from `api.py`'s own module docstring, which still read "the two map kinds this repo carries". …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.9.1: the two debts the roadmap kept naming
item.description: Both of these were known, written down, and carried anyway — one in a docstring, one in the README's own roadmap. Neither was hard; they were just never the thing in front of us. Fixed **Lake Urmia was drawn at an extent the world no longer has.** Natural Earth carries it near its historic ~4 200 km², and it has repeatedly fallen below a fifth of that since the 2010s. The two existing escape hatches both lie about it: `lakes.skip` hides the question, and `lakes.former` asserts a disappearance that has not happened — the lake still exists, at a fraction of the polygon on file. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.9.0: drawing how sure you are, and fitting in a column
item.description: Two questions, asked one after the other. First: this generator could draw *what* an analyst assessed but had no way to draw *how sure they were*, and a map that cannot say "probably" says "certainly" by default. Second: what changes when the deliverable is not the map but the article the map illustrates. Both were answered by reading the people who publish this kind of map for a living — ISW, ACLED, Liveuamap on the assessment side, the graphics desks on the page side — and by reading the two tools that already write SVG from geodata, svgis and mapshaper. Then by rendering plates at the widths those desks actually publish at and looking at what broke. What the plate knows, and how well …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.8.0: the plate says what it is, and where it is going
item.description: The whole of this release came out of rendering real plates and looking at them. Two current-affairs maps were built as tests — Sudan's east-west partition and who holds the Kivus — and every item below is something one of them exposed. Added **Axes of advance.** Areas of control say where the line *is*; nothing said which way it was moving, and without that a plate can only describe a frozen moment. `arrows:` takes a list of `line` coordinates and draws a tapered, white-cased arrow along a Catmull-Rom curve through them — the shaft is a filled outline rather than a stroke, because a stroke is one width for its whole length and a shaft that thickens towards the point is the mark that carries direction without a caption. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.7.0: a planet with rivers, cities and terrain that is computed
item.description: Added **Cities on every map, by default.** A map of the Earth with nobody on it is a map of an empty planet: a reader could see where the Andes are and not where Lima is, and had no anchor for the scale of what they were looking at. Chosen by Natural Earth's cartographic prominence, **not** by "is it a capital" — that is a political list and it omits New York, Mumbai, São Paulo, Shanghai, Los Angeles and Karachi, six of the world's twelve largest. The vendored list carries 1 251 places, 1 051 of which are not capitals, and the selection widens as the map zooms in because prominence is exactly the question "does this belong at this scale". …

item.title: sprezzature 1.3.7: the maps skill says what a map now carries on its own
item.description: Added **A map is of a populated planet by default.** `sprezzature-maps` 0.7.0 puts cities, rivers and computed relief on every map without being asked, so the skill now leads with what arrives on its own and how to switch each off — the reverse of the previous posture, where everything was a mode. The two rules an agent needs from it: cities are chosen by cartographic prominence rather than by "is it a capital", which is a political list that omits six of the world's twelve largest; and a label in the way is dropped, never moved, because a name nudged clear of its dot points at the wrong place and the reader cannot tell. If a wanted name is missing, widen the selection or place it by hand — hand-placed names always win. Fixed The `all` extra floored `sprezzature-maps` at 0.6.0.

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.6.0: a mistyped config key is refused, not ignored
item.description: Fixed **A one-letter slip in a situation-map config silently dropped whatever it configured.** The plate is driven by two dozen optional keys, hand-edited in YAML, and an unrecognised key was simply never read. `canvas_widthl` rendered at the default width without a word. A slip on `areas_of_control` would have dropped an entire layer — and the plate would still have looked like a finished intelligence product, which is the worst possible response to a typo: the map is wrong and nothing says so. `validate_config` refuses any key the generator does not read, and names the closest known one, because the realistic cause is a typo and the realistic fix is one character. A missing `region` now explains what a region is instead of raising a bare `KeyError` from deep inside the layout code. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.5.0: no class may straddle zero on a diverging ramp
item.description: Fixed **A classed diverging map could paint a recession the colour of growth.** A diverging scale exists to show which side of the midpoint a value falls on, and 0.3.0's classification had nothing stopping a class from spanning it. The class then takes the colour of its own centre: a quantile class holding −1.2 and +2.9 came out `#CFDBEC`, a blue from the positive side, for both. Not a theoretical risk. Over 3 986 random datasets with values of both signs, a class straddled zero in 2 537 of them under `quantile`, 1 573 under `jenks`, 1 203 under `headtail` and 985 under `equal`. After the fix: none, by any method. …

item.title: sprezzature 1.3.6: the maps skill gains the two failures classing brought with it
item.description: Added **The diverging rule.** A classed diverging map could paint a recession the colour of growth — a class spanning zero takes the colour of its own centre. `sprezzature-maps` 0.5.0 makes zero a boundary; the skill now says why that rule exists, because an agent choosing `classes` on growth rates or anomalies needs to know the trap was there and is closed. **Config keys are validated.** 0.6.0 refuses a situation-map key the generator does not read, naming the closest known one. The skill says so, so an agent that gets the error knows it is a typo and not a missing feature. Fixed The `all` extra floored `sprezzature-maps` at 0.4.0 while the skill documents behaviour from 0.5.0 and 0.6.0.

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.4.0: the accumulation map becomes a kind, not a script
item.description: Added **`density` is a map kind now**, on all five surfaces: `make_density()`, `make-map density`, `POST /v1/density`, the `render_density` MCP tool, and a row in the skill. It shipped in 0.2.0 as `scripts/make_density.py` — a file somebody had to run by hand. Not exported, no CLI kind, no route, and absent from `list_kinds`, so the map existed in the repository and nowhere else. A map nobody can reach is a map this package does not have. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.3.0: the choropleth can finally be classed, and says how
item.description: Added **`classes` and `method` on the choropleth, across all five surfaces.** The generator had one rule for turning numbers into colours: stretch the ramp linearly from the smallest value to the largest. That is unclassed equal interval, and cartography is unanimous that it is the weakest choice for the right-skewed data indicators are made of. Measured rather than asserted: on GDP per head for twenty countries it puts nine of them in the bottom quarter of the ramp, and of the pairs a five-class quantile separates, four come out closer than the eye can resolve — India, at ten times Burundi's figure, lands 0.0115 apart in OKLab where 0.02 is the threshold. Four methods, because no default is right for every dataset: `quantile` — equal count per class. Supports ranking; flattens skew by construction, and two very different values can share a class. …

item.title: sprezzature-maps 0.2.0: four modes, a provenance block, and a first publication
item.description: Added **A night plate**, as a mode and nothing more — the same geography, read in the dark. **Rivers tapered by prominence**, opt-in. A river that matters is drawn thicker than one that does not, which is the only reason to draw rivers on a situation plate at all. **An accumulation map** (`scripts/make_density.py`), where the data draws the geography: point events binned to a luminous field, no coastline, no border, no graticule. The United States appears because events fell on it. Vector, binned, one path per level — measured rather than guessed: on 381,406 points a rect per cell costs 972 KB, quantising the ramp and merging each level into one path lands at ~100 KB in ten paths, and past ~260 bins the field becomes grain, so the visual limit arrives before the size limit. …

item.title: sprezzature-figures 2.3.0: a figure proved legible without a vision model
item.description: Added **`check_render()` — the questions the eyeball loop asks, answered from the SVG source.** The Ralph Eyeball Loop decides "does this read?" by showing the PNG to a vision model, and that answer only exists where such a model does. A service with a text-only LLM, or none, still ships figures and cannot have someone look at each one. This asks the same questions from the markup and answers them the same way every time: do labels collide, does text run off the canvas, did a generator's demo chrome ("Region", "Quarterly figures") survive into a real render, is a dark figure actually dark or is there a light card in the middle of it, is the caller's title on the figure, is there an accessible title and description. …

item.title: sprezzature-figures 2.2.0: a chart you were sent, tools an agent can choose between, and a dark canvas
item.description: Added **`dark=True` — the same figure, drawn for a dark canvas.** The full-canvas white rectangle is dropped so the figure sits transparent on whatever is behind it, and the chrome (ink, secondary text, gridlines) is lightened. Series colours are untouched, and so is the white that carries meaning — a label printed on a coloured bar. Reachable as `make_figure(..., dark=True)`, `--dark` on the CLI, and `to_dark()` for an SVG you already have. Applied centrally in `make_figure` for SVG output and popped before the generator runs, so no generator learns a second palette. The light rendering is unchanged byte for byte. …

item.title: sprezzature-audio 1.1.0: five surfaces, and the headline an MCP host shows
item.description: Fixed `translate_captions.py` and `name_from_transcript.py` imported `best_engine_ai_helper.llm.chat` at module level, even though `best-engine-ai-helper` is only declared in the `translate` extra, not a base dependency. `pip install sprezzature-audio` with no extras broke both scripts' `--help` with a `ModuleNotFoundError`, before argument parsing even ran. The import now happens inside the function that needs it, matching the deferred-import policy every other script in this project already follows for NeMo, pywhispercpp, and numpy. …

item.title: sprezzature-accessibility 1.0.2: the rule count on the package page itself
